A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same unlearning evaluation framework despite the changed title and publication format. Their main texts, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–C are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original experiments comparing unlearning metrics and algorithms, including vision benchmarks, sensitivity studies and certified removal on a binary MNIST task.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experiments and adds SST5 text-classification results using BERT in Appendix C.4, Table 7.

M1.justification: The inference game, Unlearning Quality metric, SWAP construction and weak-adversary approximation remain unchanged. BERT is an added evaluation target, not a modification of the proposed method.

E1.justification: v3 evaluates CIFAR10, CIFAR100 and MNIST, including binary MNIST classification. v4 retains this coverage and adds five-class SST5 text classification, substantially extending the evaluated domain beyond vision.

E2.justification: The IC and MIA-score comparisons retain their comparator sets. The new SST5 column evaluates the same six unlearning methods already present in v3 Table 7; newly cited cryptographic work is not experimentally compared.

E3.justification: The added SST5 experiment introduces BERT as the target model with an unlearning fraction of 0.1. Existing vision and linear-model protocols, including their splits, metrics, training settings and privacy budgets, remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The dataset-size, forgetting-fraction, architecture, augmentation and linear-model analyses already appear in v3. The size and fraction studies move into v4 Section 4.2; SST5 adds benchmark coverage rather than a separate robustness or ablation analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions retain three-model averaging per split, existing standard-deviation reporting and standard-error threshold symbols. The SST5 entries follow the existing ± reporting practice without newly specified run counts or statistical procedures.

E6.justification: Table 7 adds six SST5 results, including SSD at 0.592 ± 0.011 and NEGGRAD at 0.376 ± 0.017. All pre-existing tabulated values and uncertainty entries are retained after matching renumbered tables; these are new-setting results, not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The zero-grounding and certified-removal guarantees, SWAP properties, counterexamples and appendix proofs are retained. A local probability-notation edit in the certified-removal proof does not change its argument or bound.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: a cryptographic evaluation game, provable metric properties and an efficient SWAP approximation. The stronger-sounding title and additional experiment do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: New Remark 4.2 distinguishes application cost from expensive DP-based validation. v4 omits the earlier explanation of representing unequal-size splits through zero sensitivity weights. Table 7 also extends the dataset-difficulty interpretation to SST5, although the different BERT and ResNet settings do not establish that comparison.

D1.justification: Appendix C.4 adds brief SST5 configuration information, including BERT and an unlearning fraction of 0.1, but no BERT-specific training recipe. CIFAR100 and MNIST license disclosures from v3 Section 4.4 are omitted; existing hardware, runtimes and ResNet hyperparameters remain.

R1.justification: Appendix A adds comparisons with Chourasia and Shah (2023) and Brimhall et al. (2025), distinguishing their threat models and cryptographic formulations. References for BERT and SST5 are also added; the broader research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: v4 changes the title and author-name styling, moves cryptographic background into Appendix B.1, brings sensitivity motivation into Section 3.2 and promotes existing ablations into Section 4.2. These are localized revisions; most prose and the overall argument remain stable.

P2.justification: The paper receives a document-wide NeurIPS reformatting, changing typography, text width, running headers and equation layout. Former appendix Tables 4–5 become main-text Tables 1–2, the DP table gains surrounding text, and Table 7 gains an SST5 column. Figure 1 retains its content.

improvement.justification: SST5/BERT provides initial empirical support beyond v3's vision-only evaluation, while Remark 4.2 and Appendix A clarify computational cost and distinctions from related cryptographic work. These yield a modest net improvement. Sparse BERT training details and the unsupported cross-dataset difficulty interpretation in Table 7 limit the benefit.
